buildLab.title: Wire it up
growthStory.title: How my project grew
buildLab.lede: Tap a metal dot, then tap another dot to join them with a wire. Tap a wire to remove it. Turn on the sun to test.
lab.goal.0: The panel sits above the plant. Wire the panel to the motor so the fan blows air toward the plant.
lab.goal.1: Wire the panel to the LED so it lights up next to the plant.
lab.goal.2: Use the one panel above the plant to run the fan and the LED at the same time.
lab.goal.3: Wire the panel to the water pump so it sends water from the tank through the tube to the plant.
lab.real.0: Clip the red wire from the large panel to one motor tab and the black wire to the other. Take it into direct sun. If the air blows the wrong way, swap the two clips.
lab.real.1: Clip red to the LED’s longer leg and black to the shorter leg. If it stays dark in full sun, flip the clips. The LED will not break.
lab.real.2: Join all the reds together (panel, motor, LED long leg) and all the blacks together. One alligator clip can hold two wires. If your panel says 5 V or more, add a 100–220 Ω resistor to the LED.
lab.real.3: Put the mini pump in a cup of water and run its tube into the pot. Clip red to the pump’s red (+) wire and black to its black (−) wire. A pump needs strong sun, so use the big panel. Keep the panel and clips up high and dry.
lab.status.pickSecond: Now tap the dot you want to connect to.
lab.status.start: Tap a dot to start a wire.
lab.status.turnOnSun: Turn on the sun to test your wires.
lab.status.short: Short circuit! The + and − of the panel are joined directly, so the power skips the parts. Remove that wire.
lab.status.fanOk: It works! The air blows toward the plant.
lab.status.fanBackwards: The fan spins, but the air blows away from the plant. A motor has no wrong way, so swap the two wires.
lab.status.fanNothing: Nothing yet. The motor needs one wire from + and one wire from −.
lab.status.ledOk: It glows! Red to the long leg, black to the short leg.
lab.status.ledBackwards: Still dark. An LED only works one way: + goes to the long leg. Swap the wires.
lab.status.ledNothing: Nothing yet. The LED needs one wire from + and one from −.
lab.status.pumpOk: Water is flowing! The pump moves water from the tank to the plant while the sun shines.
lab.status.pumpBackwards: The pump hums but only a trickle comes out. Most mini pumps have a + and a − side. Swap the wires.
lab.status.pumpNothing: Nothing yet. The pump needs one wire from + and one wire from −.
lab.status.bothOk: Both run from one panel! This is a parallel circuit: each part has its own path to + and −.
lab.status.bothFanOnly: The fan runs, but the LED is dark. Give the other part its own + and − path too.
lab.status.bothLedOnly: The LED glows, but the fan is still. Give the other part its own + and − path too.
lab.status.bothLedBackwards: The LED is turned around: + must reach the long leg.
lab.status.bothSeries: Looks like a chain (series). In a chain the LED blocks most of the current, so the fan cannot start. Connect each part straight to + and −.
lab.status.bothNothing: Connect both parts to the panel.

home.title: Grow food. Make energy. Share the same sun.
home.lede: In Same Sun you build a mini agrivoltaic system: a small solar panel set above a plant, so one sunny spot makes energy and grows food. Test your ideas here, then try them on your real kit.
home.dq: How can one sunny space grow food and make energy at the same time?
home.heroLabel: A solar panel on posts above a seedling in a pot, with a small fan beside it
home.whatTitle: What is a mini agrivoltaic system?
home.panelText: A small solar panel turns sunlight into electricity that lights an LED or spins a tiny fan.
home.plantsText: Seedlings grow in the panel’s shade, which can shelter them from desert heat.
home.designText: You choose panel size, height and plant, then test what works and why.
home.howLede: Three parts. Each one matches something you do with your real kit.
home.step1Text: Pick a plant and a panel, guess what will happen, then watch a sunny day in under a minute.
home.step2Text: Connect the panel to the fan and LED. Red goes to +, black goes to −.
home.step3Text: Add a photo and a few words each time you work on your project, then open them again any time.
sunDay.title: Can one sunny spot grow food and make energy?
sunDay.lede: Set up your panels above a seedling, guess what will happen, then run a sunny Arizona day and see how your plant and your panel did.

predict.title: Make a prediction
predict.prompt: Compared with the same plant in full sun with no panel, your plant will grow…
predict.why.pump: the pump keeps the soil wet
results.ref: A plot with no panel scores {fs}. Beat it by sharing the sun.
results.note: The black line on Food marks a plant in full sun with no panel. Food is out of a perfect day; Energy is out of the best panel setup.
results.skipped: You skipped the prediction this time.
results.what: Your {crop} grew {food}% of a perfect {span}. A full-sun plant grew {fs}%. Your panel made {wh} Wh, which is {energy}% of the best setup.
controls.group1: 1 · Pick a plant and a day
controls.panelHint: Bigger panels make more energy, and more shade.
controls.heightHint: A high panel lets more light in from the sides.
controls.waterPump: The pump waters the plant by itself when the soil gets dry. It needs strong sun and a big panel.
controls.waterHand: Without the pump, you water the plant once each morning.
controls.foot: Prototype numbers are made up to feel right, not measured. The team will tune them with the real kit.
cropHint.lettuce: Likes cool weather and some shade.
cropHint.chili: Loves sun and handles heat well.
challenge.heat.name: Challenge 1: Beat the heat
challenge.heat.goal: Heat wave week with basil. Grow at least twice as much as basil with no panel.
challenge.heat.pass: Your basil grew more than twice the no-panel basil.
challenge.heat.fail: Your basil needs more protection from the heat.
challenge.fan.name: Challenge 2: Fan all afternoon
challenge.fan.goal: Sunny day. Keep the fan spinning every hour from noon to 5 pm, and grow at least as much as a plant with no panel.
challenge.fan.pass: The fan ran all afternoon and the plant kept up.
challenge.fan.fail: The fan stopped in the afternoon, or the plant fell behind.
challenge.tank.name: Challenge 3: Water by itself all week
challenge.tank.goal: Sunny week with the pump and no hand watering. The soil may be dry for 30 hours at most.
challenge.tank.pass: The soil stayed just right all week.
challenge.tank.fail: The soil got too dry. Try slowing down how fast it dries.
rules.soggy.why: The soil stayed soggy for {soggy} hours. Too much water makes roots soggy, and soggy roots grow slowly.
rules.soggy.next: How could the pump water only when the soil is dry?
rules.soggy.hint.0: Look at the watering choices again.
rules.soggy.hint.1: The Smart pump checks the soil before it waters.
rules.soggy.hint.2: Try Smart pump with the setting near 45%.
rules.tankEmpty.why: The tank ran dry on day {day} at {hour}:00, then the soil dried out.
rules.tankEmpty.next: How could the same water last longer?
rules.tankEmpty.hint.0: Where does the water go on a hot day?
rules.tankEmpty.hint.1: Shade slows drying, so the same water lasts longer.
rules.tankEmpty.hint.2: Try both panels with the pump on.
rules.dry.why: The soil got too dry for {dry} sunny hours, mostly in the afternoon. Thirsty plants stop growing.
rules.dry.next: What would slow the soil from drying, or add water during the day?
rules.dry.hint.0: Where does the water go on a hot afternoon?
rules.dry.hint.1: Shade slows drying. The pump can water while the sun shines.
rules.dry.hint.2: Turn on the pump, and use a big panel to power it.
rules.hot.why: Leaves got hotter than {stress} °F for {hot} hours. {crop} gets stressed above that.
rules.hot.next: What could keep the leaves cooler during the hottest hours?
rules.hot.hint.0: When is the sun strongest? What is above the plant then?
rules.hot.hint.1: More shade and a running fan both cool the leaves.
rules.hot.hint.2: Try a big panel or both panels, with the fan on.
rules.lowLight.why: Your {crop} got about {light}% of the sun under the panels, and it wanted more light to grow fast.
rules.lowLight.next: How could you give the plant more light and still make energy?
rules.lowLight.hint.0: Light can sneak in from the sides.
rules.lowLight.hint.1: A high panel lets more side light in. A smaller panel makes less shade.
rules.lowLight.hint.2: Try the panel set high, or the small panel.
rules.fanWeak.why: The fan only ran about {hours} hours a day. The panel did not make enough power for it most of the day.
rules.fanWeak.next: How could your panel make more power?
rules.fanWeak.hint.1: The fan needs more power than a small panel makes in the morning and evening.
rules.fanWeak.hint.2: Try the big panel or both panels.
rules.lowEnergy.why: Your panel made {energy}% of the energy the best setup can make.
rules.lowEnergy.next: Can you make more energy and still keep the plant happy?
rules.lowEnergy.hint.0: Which panel catches the most sun?
rules.lowEnergy.hint.1: More panel area means more energy, but also more shade.
rules.noPanel.why: With no panel, the plant gets all the sun and you make no energy.
rules.noPanel.next: What happens to the plant if you add a panel above it?
rules.noPanel.hint.0: Shade can help or hurt. It depends on the plant and the heat.
rules.noPanel.hint.1: Try a small panel first, then compare.
rules.noPanel.hint.2: Try the big panel set high.
rules.balanced.why: A good balance: the plant stayed comfortable and the panel made {energy}% of the best energy.
rules.balanced.next: Can you raise one score without dropping the other?
rules.balanced.hint.0: Change just one thing, then run again and compare.
rules.balanced.hint.1: Try the other panel height, or a different panel size.
rules.balanced.hint.2: Compare Big + high with Both + high.
